current_docstring_summary: Outer-loop, U_prob-based (NOT Z_scaled-based) per-community domain-balance check. Builds soc_facets/sem_facets lists restricted to facets present in presence_masks with sum()>0 and present in U_prob, using FACET_DOMAIN to classify each facet as social/semantic. For each domain, computes an entity-count-weighted mean U_prob row over live entities only (nested _weighted_share, line 1408) across that domain's live facets. r_k = soc_share/(soc_share+sem_share+eps) per community k; dev_k = |r_k-0.5|; penalty = mean_k(max(0, dev_k - tol)^2). Returns a 2-tuple (domain_balance_pen: float, mean_dev_k: float), both already native Python float (no separate float() cast needed at call site since np.mean(...) results are cast inline).
notable_facts: Returns (0.0, 0.0) if either soc_facets or sem_facets end up empty, or if either _weighted_share() returns None (total live-entity weight 0) — i.e. it silently no-ops to zero penalty rather than raising, in configs where one domain has no live facets.

tol default is DOMAIN_BALANCE_TOL=0.15; per CLAUDE.md this is explicitly NOT in Optuna's search space (never passed a non-default tol anywhere in the file — grep confirms only one call site, evaluate_complete_solution line 1516-1519, uses the default).

Called exactly once in the whole file: inside evaluate_complete_solution (line 1516), reusing U_prob and presence_masks already computed there for Section 4 (evaluate_socio_semantic_reality) rather than recomputing them.

domain_balance_pen is summed UNCONDITIONALLY into sociological_penalty at line 1521, regardless of the separate in-loop lambda_domain_balance weight (which defaults to 0.0 and is architecturally independent of this outer-loop function).
Units: r_k and dev_k are dimensionless probability-mass shares (entity-count-weighted mean of L1 row-normalized U_prob rows), not raw counts.

Per CLAUDE.md's own ticket 82/E3 record (not this agent's judgment, just noting the doc's own claim for cross-reference): a planted-structure test found this formula's output (dev_k) does not track true planted domain imbalance on this corpus — but the code of evaluate_domain_balance itself, read in isolation, is internally consistent with its docstring's stated formula.

current_docstring_summary: No docstring (anonymous nested helper). Computes total_w = sum of live-entity counts across the given facets (presence_masks[f].sum()); for each facet, takes the live-entity subset of U_prob[f], computes its column-wise mean (mean over rows/entities, per community k), weights that per-facet mean by the facet's live-entity count, sums across facets, and divides by total_w. Returns None if total_w is 0 or if no facet contributed (acc stays None); otherwise returns a length-K ndarray of the entity-count-weighted mean U_prob profile for that set of facets.
notable_facts: This is entity-count weighting (D2 in CLAUDE.md ticket 82), not equal-per-facet weighting — a facet with more live entities dominates the domain-level average more, algebraically equivalent to pooling all live entities in the domain and taking one grand mean.

Only used inside evaluate_domain_balance (called twice per invocation: once for soc_facets, once for sem_facets). Not reused elsewhere in the file — the differentiable in-loop analog (_db_domain_share, ~line 618) is a separately written torch version, not a call to this function (by design, per the file's own comments, to keep Module 2/Module 3 separate).

current_signature_or_value: def evaluate_complete_solution(U_final, Z_final, U_scales_out, raw_data, soc_keys, sem_keys, anchor_keys, max_monopoly, entropy_threshold, target_coherence):
current_docstring_summary: Single-line docstring only ("Computes every outer-loop sociological metric from a solved model. This function is the single source of truth for sociological evaluation."). Body: converts U_final/Z_final tensors to numpy if needed; builds active_matrices set; rebuilds presence_masks fresh via build_presence_masks(raw_data, soc_keys, sem_keys); computes U_prob via compute_probability_distributions(U_numpy); calls evaluate_dimensional_collapse(U_final=U_numpy, Z_final=Z_numpy) — NOTE: called with only 2 args, using its own defaults for max_share_threshold/structure_threshold, NOT this function's own entropy_threshold parameter; calls evaluate_topological_coherence(Z_numpy, target_coherence, frozenset(anchor_keys)); calls evaluate_socio_semantic_reality(U_prob, raw_data, active_matrices_set, max_monopoly, presence_masks); calls evaluate_domain_balance(U_prob, presence_masks) reusing U_prob/presence_masks already computed. sociological_penalty = collapse_pen + coherence_pen + socio_semantic_pen + domain_balance_pen (line 1521) — FOUR terms, unweighted (no lambda multipliers), summed unconditionally. Returns a dict with exactly 8 keys: collapse_pen, collapse_score, coherence_pen, weakest_coherence, semantic_pen, domain_balance_pen, mean_dev_k, sociological_penalty.
notable_facts: sociological_penalty is composed of 4 unweighted terms (collapse_pen + coherence_pen + socio_semantic_pen(returned under dict key 'semantic_pen') + domain_balance_pen), confirmed directly at line 1521. Any doc claiming 3 terms is describing a pre-ticket-82-E2 state.

The function's own parameters U_scales_out and entropy_threshold are VESTIGIAL for this call (per an explicit in-code comment at ~line 1484-1491) — kept only so the external signature doesn't change across its 3 call sites (CLAUDE.md §3 policy), but neither value is actually forwarded into evaluate_dimensional_collapse anymore (that function uses its own MAX_SHARE_THRESHOLD/STRUCTURE_SCORE_THRESHOLD module defaults, not entropy_threshold).
max_monopoly and target_coherence, by contrast, ARE actively used (forwarded to evaluate_socio_semantic_reality and evaluate_topological_coherence respectively).

All 8 dict values are already native Python floats by the time they reach this dict, since each sub-function (evaluate_dimensional_collapse, evaluate_topological_coherence, evaluate_socio_semantic_reality, evaluate_domain_balance) casts to float at its own return.

current_docstring_summary: Computes community mass from Z_scaled (relation-level, permutation-corrected via _hungarian_relabel_relation/_relation_community_share), NOT from U_scales (U_scales is an undetermined free gauge direction, per the docstring's own citation of ticket 79). For each relation in Z_final, gets a per-community reconstruction-space share vector via _relation_community_share; averages these vectors across all active relations with EQUAL weight (no nnz-weighting, no structure_score-weighting, no recon-quality-weighting — all three were tested and rejected per the docstring); renormalizes the K-length averaged vector to sum to 1 (falling back to uniform 1/K if total_share <= 1e-15). max_share = the max of this normalized vector. collapse_pen = squared ceiling penalty: (max(0, max_share - max_share_threshold) / (1 - max_share_threshold))^2. Returns (collapse_pen: float, max_share: float) — the second return value is documented as reusing the dict key name 'collapse_score' downstream even though its MEANING changed (was normalized_entropy, now max_share).
notable_facts: Does NOT take U_scales_out as an argument at all (unlike its historical/older version implied by some docs) — signature is only (U_final, Z_final, max_share_threshold, structure_threshold).

Called from evaluate_complete_solution with ONLY 2 positional/keyword args (U_final=U_numpy, Z_final=Z_numpy) — max_share_threshold and structure_threshold use their module-constant defaults every time in production; nothing in the file overrides them at the call site.

The local variable named `community_share` inside this function (line 1013) is NOT a standalone function — it is a local ndarray variable, the mean-then-renormalized per-community share vector. Any doc reference to a function/symbol literally named `community_share_vector` does not correspond to this variable (see F-CHUNK13V9-NOTFOUND-01 — that exact name has zero hits anywhere in this file).
Guards K<2 and empty Z_final by returning (0.0, 1.0) immediately — no penalty, max_share pinned to 1.0 (this is a degenerate/trivial-case return, not a real measurement).

Cross-relation conflicts are NOT resolved: each relation is corrected independently via _hungarian_relabel_relation; the docstring explicitly states this function does not detect or resolve disagreement between multiple relations sharing a non-leaf facet.

current_docstring_summary: Given a K x K relation core matrix Z, uses scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment on -abs(Z) to find the diagonal-maximizing permutation (Hungarian algorithm). structure_score = min(matched diagonal-under-permutation entries) / max(unmatched entries). Returns (perm: list[int], trusted: bool) where trusted = structure_score > structure_threshold. If total_mass of abs(Z) is <=1e-15, short-circuits to (list(range(K)), False) (identity perm, not trusted). If max_unmatched is ~0 (no off-diagonal mass), structure_score is set to float('inf') (always trusted in that case).
notable_facts: trusted=True (structure_score > threshold) means a confidently clean relabelling exists and IS applied by callers; trusted=False means genuine mixed coupling and the raw identity permutation is used as-is — this is the interpretation stated directly in the docstring, consistent with STRUCTURE_SCORE_THRESHOLD's own comment.

structure_threshold has no default in this function's own signature — every caller must supply it explicitly. Its only caller in the file, _relation_community_share, passes through its own structure_threshold parameter, which in turn is only ever supplied the module constant STRUCTURE_SCORE_THRESHOLD by evaluate_dimensional_collapse's default.
Called only from _relation_community_share (line 920) in this file — not called directly from evaluate_complete_solution or anywhere else.

current_docstring_summary: Computes a reconstruction-space per-community share vector for one relation. Gets (perm, trusted) from _hungarian_relabel_relation; uses the corrected permutation p if trusted, else identity. Computes c_u = U_final_f1.T @ U_final_f1, c_v = U_final_f2.T @ U_final_f2, and total = trace(Z.T @ c_u @ Z @ c_v) — the relation's entire reconstructed Frobenius mass (diagonal AND off-diagonal, i.e. including cross-community interference). within[k] = Z[k, p[k]]^2 for each community k (this reduces algebraically to the within-community reconstructed mass because U_norm's columns are unit-L2 by construction). Returns within/total elementwise, or a uniform 1/K vector if total <= 1e-15.
notable_facts: This is the function CLAUDE.md's own §4.18 design section names as production's own mass mechanism for the (superseded, rejected) Z_scaled-based domain-balance draft — it is used by evaluate_dimensional_collapse (via a loop over Z_final.items()), NOT by evaluate_domain_balance (which is U_prob-based and does not call this function at all).

Chosen over a simpler diagonal-sum share specifically because it is sensitive to cross-community interference (a relation whose mass is mostly off-diagonal contributes correspondingly little share to any community, rather than being forced to sum diagonal entries to 1).
Only caller in the file: evaluate_dimensional_collapse (one call per relation in Z_final, line 1010).

current_docstring_summary: The differentiable, in-loop (torch) analog of evaluate_domain_balance's outer-loop _weighted_share. Given U_norm_dict (differentiable torch tensors, NOT U_prob), a list of facets, and a precomputed total live-entity weight w_total: for each facet, masks to live entities via the closed-over db_mask_t[f] torch bool tensor, L1-row-normalizes inline (row_sums = sum(abs(live), dim=1) + 1e-12; u_prob_live = live/row_sums — i.e. it computes an on-the-fly U_prob equivalent from U_norm rather than calling compute_probability_distributions, which is numpy-only and would break autograd), weights the facet's live-row mean by db_live_counts[f] (live-entity count), sums across facets, and divides by w_total. Returns None if facets is empty, w_total==0, or no facet contributed data.
notable_facts: This is the DIFFERENTIABLE counterpart used to build domain_balance_loss inside run_inner_solver's training loop (per-epoch), gated by lambda_domain_balance (default 0.0, read via params.get('lambda_domain_balance', 0.0) at line 572) — NOT the same code path as the outer-loop evaluate_domain_balance/_weighted_share, by explicit design (kept separate per the file's own comment at lines 604-607, to preserve the Module 2/Module 3 separation-of-concerns boundary).
Called twice per training epoch (once for db_soc_facets, once for db_sem_facets, at lines 692-693) inside the epoch loop of run_inner_solver.

The static topology it depends on (db_presence_masks, db_live_counts, db_mask_t, db_soc_facets, db_sem_facets, db_soc_total, db_sem_total) is computed ONCE before the epoch loop starts (lines 608-616), not recomputed per epoch — only the U_norm-dependent mean is recomputed each epoch.

The resulting domain_balance_loss (mean of squared dead-band excess past DOMAIN_BALANCE_TOL) is exposed unweighted in diagnostics as 'raw_domain_balance_penalty' (line 795-796) even when lambda_domain_balance=0 zeroes its contribution to total_loss/internal_soc_loss.

current_signature_or_value: def evaluate_socio_semantic_reality(U_prob, raw_data, active_matrices, max_monopoly, presence_masks=None):
current_docstring_summary: Computes a combined socio-semantic reality penalty in two parts. Part A: for each community k, propagates article-level weight W_art = U_prob['art'][:,k] outward through the active M_* relations (parent/child/cousin/atom/fringe, following the actual topology), and for each of 4 target semantic facets (core_child_he, cousin_he, core_atom, fringe_atom) compares a weighted average of the model's own U_prob loading (weighted by the propagated empirical weight) against a live-entity-masked baseline mean loading; squared-ceiling penalty when weighted_avg falls short of baseline. Part B: using the same propagated per-community weights captured as empirical_mass_capture, computes a normalized Shannon entropy per entity (how 'universal'/doxa-like a semantic node's empirical usage is) and multiplies a squared max_monopoly-ceiling penalty (on the model's own max learned U_prob loading) by that entropy — i.e. only penalizes hoarding of high-entropy/universal terms, not niche ones. Final: socio_semantic_pen = (Penalty_A + Penalty_B) / 2.0.
notable_facts: DOCSTRING/BEHAVIOR MISMATCH: the function's docstring explicitly states 'Returns: socio_semantic_pen (float)... Penalty_A (float)... Penalty_B (float)' (three named return values), but every actual return statement in the body returns a SINGLE value: `return 1.0` (the K<2 early-exit guard, line ~1144) and `return float(socio_semantic_pen)` (the normal path, line 1333). Penalty_A and Penalty_B are computed internally but never returned. The single call site (evaluate_complete_solution, line 1506) correctly assigns the return to a single variable `socio_semantic_pen = evaluate_socio_semantic_reality(...)`, i.e. the call site's usage matches the actual 1-value behavior, not the docstring's stated 3-value behavior.
The K<2 early-return path returns the bare Python literal `1.0`, not `float(1.0)` explicitly, but this is already a native float so no JSON-serializability issue.

presence_masks is optional (defaults to None) — when None, Part A's baseline and Part B's valid_mask fall back to using ALL rows (dead entities included), not just live ones. In production it is always passed (evaluate_complete_solution always supplies presence_masks), so the None-fallback path is a defined-but-effectively-unused branch in the current call graph — worth noting for anyone editing based on 'presence_masks is optional' language.

target_facets is hardcoded to exactly 4 facets: ['core_child_he', 'cousin_he', 'core_atom', 'fringe_atom'] — parent_he is NOT included (this matches the open, undecided ticket 66 in CLAUDE.md about whether to add it).

current_docstring_summary: For each active anchor relation (an anchor being any relation key present in both Z_final and the semantic_anchors frozenset), and for each community k, computes a symmetric cohesion ratio: diagonal_val / (0.5*(row_sum+col_sum)+eps), clipped to [0,1]. Averages this ratio across all active anchors for each community (the 'Mean Anchor Rule', allowing polycentric communities that are crisp at one semantic resolution but noisier at another). weakest_mean = the minimum such mean cohesion score across all K communities. coherence_pen = squared ceiling: (max(0, target_coherence - weakest_mean) / target_coherence)^2. Returns (coherence_pen: float, weakest_mean: float).
notable_facts: Returns (0.0, np.nan) immediately if no anchors from semantic_anchors are active in Z_final — this nan is only ever logged via trial.set_user_attr, and coherence_pen (0.0, not nan) is what actually feeds sociological_penalty, per the file's own resolved ticket 22 register entry.
Raises ValueError if any active anchor's Z_final entry is not shape (K,K) — a hard failure, not a soft penalty.

Per CLAUDE.md's own ticket 81 measurement (not verified independently by this extraction task, just noted for cross-reference): coherence_pen has reportedly been exactly 0.0 in every tested production cell so far, though this is a claim about historical measured behavior on specific data, not something derivable from the code alone.

current_docstring_summary: For each relation key in (soc_keys + sem_keys) present in `matrices`, looks up its two facets via RELATION_MAP, computes row_live (any nonzero entry per row, via mat.getnnz(axis=1)>0) and col_live (mat.getnnz(axis=0)>0) boolean vectors, and OR-unions these into a running per-facet mask dict across ALL relations touching that facet (not just one relation — a facet's mask is the union across every active relation that touches it).
